column1: # The ring, as placed, and nothing else.
# **Flattened from wheel59 plus #14.** This file used to be the history of
# how the ring was arrived at -- a hundred-odd swaps, rolls, presses and
# inserts, each shoving tiles that earlier lines had placed. That made an
# angle written here mean something other than what it said: placements are
# all resolved before any op runs, so `ring 14 6.74` collided with where
# #73 still was at that moment and got pushed somewhere else entirely.
# Now every tile carries the angle it is actually drawn at. To move one,
# change its number. To close a gap, subtract the gap from the tile and from
# everything you want to travel with it. Nothing moves that is not named.
#   ring <n> <deg>   on the ring, at that angle
#   in / out <n> [k] off the ring, k tiers deeper / further out
# The ring, clockwise from the top.
# **Closed up.** The seven seams below a degree are gone -- 0.380 and smaller,
# none of them a gap anybody could point at. The 1.282 degrees they held had to
# go somewhere, and it is spread evenly over the six gaps that stay, so each
# grew by about a fifth of a degree rather than one of them swallowing the lot.
# The kept gaps are the six at 1.094 and above; the distribution breaks cleanly
# there, with nothing at all between 0.380 and 1.094.
# Then turned -0.36 degrees, which is the rotation that best lines the ring up
# with the hues its blends read as. It is worth almost nothing -- mean offset
# 2.375 to 2.350 -- because the ring was already close to the best a rigid turn
# can do. What offset remains is placement, not rotation.
# **Two gaps since spent.** #7 came in for #41 and #2 went in beside it, which
# used the 1.984 at 45.3; then #15 was pulled back and took its run with it, so
# what the swap left over now sits at 61.3 instead. In the other change #18 came
# off and #54 and #86 went in after #105, in hue order, and #105, #107, #64 and
# #65 closed up around them -- 8 degrees of tile into 7.391 of room, the last
# 0.609 taken off the gap before #92, which is why that one reads 1.055.
# **No gaps at all. 360 of 360.** Ten degrees of air went into tiles over six
# rather than being spread or pushed anywhere.
# The last two rounds are the push rule doing its own arithmetic. #131 is a
# single degree, and the seventeen tiles from #92 to #116 slid anticlockwise by
# exactly that, which turned the 1.055 gap into 0.055. Then #1 is `red red red`
# and also a single degree, and the two remaining gaps came to 0.945 and 0.055
# -- exactly it, between them. So it went in against its own hue, at 34.876
# against 35.06, with #8 and the three behind it giving up 0.945 anticlockwise
# and #7 and the sixteen in front of it giving up 0.055 clockwise.
# Nothing is spare now. Every further insert costs a tile its seat.
# The 0.945 is what was left when #42 came in four degrees wider than the #9 it
# replaced: 3.637 of that came out of the gap behind it, and #21 and #50 gave up
# the last 0.363 by sliding anticlockwise into the gap in front of them.
# Off the ring: which tier each sits in.
# Rejected outright: three rings of their own, below every tier that is still
# being judged. `sink` is the only verdict that moves a tile in angle without
# seating it, and the budget is now 30 degrees rather than 10 -- which is what
# buys three rows instead of four. The number after each is the blend's
# luminance, 0 to 100; the second is what the angle cost.
# Ordered here outermost band first, which is also how they are drawn: neither,
# too light, too dark. The tier is not written down -- the band is read off the
# colour, so the file cannot disagree with the drawing about which ring a tile
# is in. The angles below are only what keeps each band to a single row, and
# the two cuts live in wheel.py.
# Solved against the painted palette, which is what gets rendered.
# Neither: rejected for something other than how light they are, so nothing
# groups them. The band to look at if the wheel ever has to say why a triple
# was dropped. It carries the widest nudges because it is the sparsest.
# Too light to carry a hue. The biggest of the three now the cut has come down
# to 63 -- `white` anywhere in a triple mostly lands here.
# Too dark to carry a hue, hard against the middle of the wheel.
